acceptanceCriteria: For each resource a test creates and deletes in teardown (after/afterEach/after(:each)/ensure/fixture finalizers in at least RSpec and one JS/TS framework), the actions performed on it are listed with lines; actions known to create dependents come from a bound source or a closed, versioned, revision-pinned side-effect declaration (action -> dependent kind, cascade flags); unknown actions keep the finding advisory and say so.

A known dependent-producing action followed by a parent delete with no dependent cleanup, or cleanup that deletes the parent before the dependent, is reported with the action line and the delete line; no finding when dependents are removed first or the parent delete is declared to cascade.

Recorded run outcomes: a prior receipt row whose teardown delete returned a conflict/validation status (e.g. 409/422) is attached to the finding with status and dependent kind when known; receipts that do not bind to the test's blob abstain.
Never claims a teardown is safe when the side-effect graph is incomplete; each rule pinned by fixture tests.
Requirements in test-source-analysis-v0.md using TSA-V0-110..119 only, with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; Closes #1168.
body: GitHub #1168. E2E tests that create a parent and delete it in teardown fail at cleanup (409/422 from FK or in-use guards) when the system under test created dependents as a side effect (confirmations, audit entries, notifications, ledger lines) that cleanup never removes. Nothing flags the risk before the run. Requested: TEARDOWN-DEPENDENT-LEFTOVER using the source dependency graph or recorded run outcomes, advisory when the side-effect graph is incomplete.
title: GH #1168: test-validity: flag teardown that deletes a parent while side-effect dependents remain (TEARDOWN-DEPENDENT-LEFTOVER)
